editions.title: Between worlds
editions.intro: Unexpected doors. Impossible places. Five little journeys somewhere new.

questions.prompt: In a hole in the ground there lived a hobbit.
options: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
questions.explanation: Tolkien introduces the comfort of a hobbit-hole before Bilbo’s unexpected adventure.

questions.prompt: A woman enters a library whose books let her experience the lives she might have lived after making different choices.
options: The Invisible Life of Addie LaRue
questions.explanation: Nora Seed explores possible versions of her life through the books in the library.

questions.prompt: A twelve-year-old travels with a satyr and a daughter of Athena to recover Zeus’s stolen lightning bolt.
questions.explanation: Percy Jackson’s first quest centres on the theft of Zeus’s master bolt.

questions.prompt: An orc retires from adventuring and tries to open a coffee shop in a city unfamiliar with coffee.
options: The House in the Cerulean Sea
The Very Secret Society of Irregular Witches
questions.explanation: Viv’s fresh start in Thune exchanges a life of fighting for coffee and community.

questions.prompt: A solitary man records a vast house of statues and ocean tides. His occasional visitor is known as the Other.
options: The Ocean at the End of the Lane
The Ten Thousand Doors of January
questions.explanation: The House and its tides are the world that Piranesi patiently documents.

editions.title: Among the shelves
editions.intro: A place to begin again. A book to get lost in. Five stories for book people.

questions.prompt: After a breakup, Takako accepts a room above her uncle’s second-hand bookshop in Tokyo and begins discovering the pleasure of reading.
questions.explanation: Takako’s new beginning unfolds around her uncle Satoru’s shop in Jimbocho.

questions.prompt: A boy in Barcelona chooses a mysterious novel from the Cemetery of Forgotten Books and becomes fascinated by its author.
questions.explanation: Daniel’s discovery of a novel by Julián Carax begins this Barcelona mystery.

questions.prompt: A historical novel follows Belle da Costa Greene as she builds J. P. Morgan’s collection of rare books and manuscripts while concealing her racial identity.

book.title: The Personal Librarian
book.author: Marie Benedict and Victoria Christopher Murray

questions.explanation: The novel draws on the life of the woman who helped create the Pierpont Morgan Library.

questions.prompt: Florence Green opens a bookshop in an East Anglian coastal town and encounters polite but determined local opposition.
questions.explanation: Florence’s attempt to bring a bookshop to Hardborough disturbs the town’s established order.

questions.prompt: A bookseller named Loveday prefers books to people and has the opening lines of favourite novels tattooed on her skin.
options: The Storied Life of A. J. Fikry
questions.explanation: Loveday Cardew’s guarded life and love of books sit at the heart of this novel.

editions.title: From page to screen
editions.intro: You may know the scene. Do you know the book behind it?

questions.prompt: A teenage girl volunteers in her younger sister’s place for a televised contest in which the participants fight to the death.
questions.explanation: Katniss volunteers when Prim is selected at the reaping.

questions.prompt: Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy March grow up together, balancing family, ambitions and limited means during the American Civil War era.
questions.explanation: The March sisters’ differing hopes and temperaments shape this family story.

questions.prompt: An island theme park brings genetically recreated dinosaurs face to face with its first visitors, with disastrous consequences.
questions.explanation: Crichton turns a dinosaur attraction into a story about technology and control.

questions.prompt: Paul Atreides arrives on the desert planet Arrakis, where a precious spice makes the planet central to an interstellar struggle.
questions.explanation: Arrakis, its spice and its people are central to Paul’s story.

questions.prompt: Connell and Marianne move from the same Irish school into university, repeatedly finding and losing their connection to one another.
questions.explanation: Rooney follows the changing relationship between Marianne and Connell across several years.

editions.title: Remarkable lives
editions.intro: Five lived experiences, told by the people who lived them.

questions.prompt: A former US First Lady reflects on her childhood on Chicago’s South Side and the experiences that eventually took her to the White House.
questions.explanation: Michelle Obama traces the personal experiences behind her public life.

questions.prompt: A South African comedian recounts growing up under apartheid as the child of a Black mother and a white father.
questions.explanation: Noah’s memoir connects his childhood, his mother and the divisions of apartheid South Africa.

questions.prompt: Raised outside formal schooling in an isolated Idaho family, a young woman eventually earns a doctorate at Cambridge.
questions.explanation: Westover describes her route into education and its effects on her family relationships.

questions.prompt: Grieving her mother and facing upheaval in her life, a novice hiker sets off alone along the Pacific Crest Trail.
questions.explanation: Strayed’s solo hike becomes the framework for a memoir of grief and rebuilding.

questions.prompt: Anthony Bourdain takes readers behind restaurant doors into the heat, long shifts and unruly culture of commercial kitchens.
questions.explanation: Bourdain writes about the working life and culture of professional cooks.

editions.title: A world apart
editions.intro: Remote shores, hidden histories and lives surrounded by water.

questions.prompt: Jim Hawkins finds a pirate’s map and sails on the Hispaniola, whose crew includes the persuasive Long John Silver.
questions.explanation: Jim’s map leads him into an expedition for Captain Flint’s buried treasure.

questions.prompt: A shipwrecked sailor builds a new life on a remote island, finding ways to feed, shelter and occupy himself over many years.
questions.explanation: Defoe’s castaway narrates the practical and emotional challenges of island life.

questions.prompt: Ten strangers accept invitations to an isolated island, where their absent hosts and a series of deaths turn the visit into a trap.
questions.explanation: Soldier Island cuts Christie’s guests off from outside help.

questions.prompt: A shipwreck survivor reaches an island where a scientist is experimenting with transforming animals into humanlike beings.
questions.explanation: Edward Prendick encounters the consequences of Moreau’s experiments.

questions.prompt: A Greek Cypriot and a Turkish Cypriot fall in love in a taverna whose fig tree bears witness to the island’s divided history.
questions.explanation: Kostas, Defne and the fig tree connect personal memory with the history of Cyprus.

editions.title: A little chemistry
editions.intro: Awkward arrangements, familiar rivals and feelings that complicate everything.

questions.prompt: The son of an American president and a British prince turn a public rivalry into a much more private relationship.
questions.explanation: Alex Claremont-Diaz and Prince Henry are the pair at the centre of this romance.

questions.prompt: Tiffy and Leon share a one-bedroom flat and the same bed at different times, leaving notes before they have ever met.
questions.explanation: Their opposite working hours make an unusual flat-sharing arrangement possible.

questions.prompt: A biology PhD student starts a fake relationship with a famously difficult professor after an impulsive kiss.
questions.explanation: Olive Smith and Adam Carlsen’s pretend relationship complicates their academic lives.

questions.prompt: Literary agent Nora visits a small North Carolina town with her sister, only to keep encountering editor Charlie Lastra.
options: The Bookish Life of Nina Hill
questions.explanation: Nora’s trip to Sunshine Falls repeatedly brings her together with a familiar editor.

questions.prompt: Lucy Hutton and Joshua Templeman share an office at a publishing company and compete for the same promotion.
questions.explanation: Lucy and Joshua’s workplace rivalry drives this romantic comedy.

editions.title: Wild and wonderful
editions.intro: Fungi, forests, feathers and the lives unfolding around us.

questions.prompt: A botanist brings plant science into conversation with Indigenous knowledge, gratitude and reciprocity with the living world.
questions.explanation: Kimmerer combines her botanical training with knowledge from her Indigenous heritage.

questions.prompt: A biologist explores fungi, from yeasts and lichens to networks that help shape ecosystems.
questions.explanation: Sheldrake centres fungi and their relationships with other forms of life.

questions.prompt: After her father’s death, a writer turns to training a goshawk named Mabel.
questions.explanation: Macdonald intertwines grief, falconry and her relationship with Mabel.

questions.prompt: An author gets to know octopuses at an aquarium while exploring their behaviour and the possibilities of animal consciousness.
questions.explanation: Montgomery’s encounters with octopuses guide this work of nonfiction.

questions.prompt: A forester invites readers to consider the relationships, survival strategies and social lives of trees.
questions.explanation: Wohlleben draws on his forestry experience to examine life in the forest.

editions.title: Old myths, new voices
editions.intro: Familiar legends, seen through the people at their edges.

questions.prompt: A daughter of Helios develops a gift for witchcraft and makes a life on the island of Aeaea.
questions.explanation: Miller gives the witch encountered in the Odyssey a story of her own.

questions.prompt: Patroclus tells the story of his bond with Achilles as their lives move towards the Trojan War.
questions.explanation: Patroclus’s perspective centres the relationship behind Achilles’s legendary reputation.

questions.prompt: A princess of Crete helps Theseus face the Minotaur, setting in motion a life beyond the labyrinth.
questions.explanation: Saint revisits the myth through Ariadne and the women around her.

questions.prompt: Odysseus’s wife and her twelve maids revisit their part in the story usually told about his long journey home.
questions.explanation: Atwood gives Penelope and the maids a chance to question the familiar account.

questions.prompt: A woman who barely speaks in Virgil’s Aeneid becomes the narrator of her own life and her connection to Aeneas.
questions.explanation: Le Guin develops the voice of the Latin princess from Virgil’s epic.

editions.title: Stories from Portugal
editions.intro: Five voices and stories with Portuguese roots.

questions.prompt: An unexplained epidemic of white blindness spreads through a city, leading the authorities to quarantine the first affected people.
questions.explanation: Saramago uses a sudden loss of sight to explore how people behave towards one another.

questions.prompt: Fragments attributed to Lisbon bookkeeper Bernardo Soares turn ordinary working life into reflections on dreams, identity and existence.
options: The Notebooks of Malte Laurids Brigge
The Year of the Death of Ricardo Reis
questions.explanation: Pessoa’s fragmentary work is closely associated with the voice of Bernardo Soares.

questions.prompt: The fortunes of a wealthy Portuguese family, including the young doctor Carlos da Maia, unfold against nineteenth-century Lisbon society.
questions.explanation: The Maia family gives Queirós a way to examine several generations and their social world.

questions.prompt: Fifteen-year-old Rui leaves Angola with his family in 1975 and starts an uncertain new life in a hotel near Lisbon.
questions.explanation: Cardoso follows displacement and family life through Rui’s adolescent perspective.

questions.prompt: A woman revisits the events surrounding her marriage to a Portuguese military officer in Mozambique, questioning how that past has been told.
options: The Wind Whistling in the Cranes
The Land at the End of the World
questions.explanation: Jorge returns to a colonial wartime setting through Eva Lopo’s recollections.

editions.title: Out of time
editions.intro: A café, a doorway, a letter. Five ways to slip out of the present.

questions.prompt: A small Tokyo café lets its visitors travel into the past, provided they follow strict rules and return before their drink cools.
questions.explanation: The café’s time-travel offer is shaped by a very particular deadline.

questions.prompt: Henry’s involuntary journeys through time make his relationship with artist Clare unfold in an unusual order.
options: The First Fifteen Lives of Harry August
questions.explanation: Henry and Clare experience their shared life from different points in time.

questions.prompt: An English teacher discovers a passage into the past and takes on the task of preventing John F. Kennedy’s assassination.
questions.explanation: Jake Epping’s mission gives King’s time-travel novel its date-shaped title.

questions.prompt: Dana, a Black writer living in the 1970s, is repeatedly pulled into the world of a plantation in pre-Civil War Maryland.
questions.explanation: Butler connects Dana’s present to the lives and power structures of the American past.

questions.prompt: Two agents on opposing sides of a war across possible futures begin leaving each other letters.
options: This Is How You Lose the Time War
The Rise and Fall of D.O.D.O.

book.title: This Is How You Lose the Time War
book.author: Amal El-Mohtar and Max Gladstone

questions.explanation: The correspondence between Red and Blue becomes the centre of this novella.

editions.title: Behind closed doors
editions.intro: Strange houses, uneasy visitors and the things left unspoken.

questions.prompt: A young English solicitor visits a Transylvanian count whose plans will eventually bring a vampire to England.
questions.explanation: Jonathan Harker’s journey to the Count’s castle begins the novel’s gathering of journals and letters.

questions.prompt: A young scientist creates a living being and recoils from the creature he has brought into the world.
options: The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
questions.explanation: Victor Frankenstein’s creation and rejection of the creature drive Shelley’s novel.

questions.prompt: A new bride arrives at Manderley and finds her married life overshadowed by the memory of her husband’s first wife.
questions.explanation: The unnamed second Mrs de Winter encounters a household still shaped by Rebecca.

questions.prompt: Noemí travels to an isolated English-style mansion in Mexico after receiving a disturbing letter from her newly married cousin.
questions.explanation: Noemí’s visit to High Place begins with concern for her cousin Catalina.

questions.prompt: Merricat, her sister Constance and their uncle live apart from a hostile village after a tragedy in the Blackwood family.
options: We Have Always Lived in the Castle

book.title: We Have Always Lived in the Castle
book.author: Shirley Jackson

questions.explanation: The isolated Blackwood household is the setting for Merricat’s unsettling account.

editions.title: Dear reader
editions.intro: Private pages, distant friends and stories told one entry at a time.

questions.prompt: A Jewish teenager records daily life while hiding with her family in Amsterdam during the Nazi occupation.
options: The Diary of a Young Girl

book.title: The Diary of a Young Girl
book.author: Anne Frank

questions.explanation: Anne Frank’s diary records the experiences of a young person living in hiding.

questions.prompt: Charlie tells an unnamed friend about his first year of high school through letters, as new friendships draw him out of the sidelines.
options: The Perks of Being a Wallflower
Aristotle and Dante Discover the Secrets of the Universe

book.title: The Perks of Being a Wallflower
book.author: Stephen Chbosky

questions.explanation: Charlie’s letters give the novel its intimate account of adolescence and friendship.

questions.prompt: After the Second World War, writer Juliet Ashton exchanges letters with members of a book club formed on occupied Guernsey.
options: The Guernsey Literary and Potato Peel Pie Society

book.title: The Guernsey Literary and Potato Peel Pie Society
book.author: Mary Ann Shaffer and Annie Barrows

questions.explanation: The letters bring Juliet into contact with an island community and its wartime history.

questions.prompt: Celie’s letters to God and to her sister Nettie trace her life in the American South and her search for independence.
options: I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings
questions.explanation: Walker uses Celie’s letters to centre her voice and changing relationships.

questions.prompt: London clerk Charles Pooter records domestic mishaps, social embarrassments and his hopes of being taken seriously.
options: The Diary of a Provincial Lady
questions.explanation: The Grossmiths turn Pooter’s daily entries into a comedy of ordinary Victorian life.

editions.title: Beyond the stars
editions.intro: Stranded astronauts, unlikely crews and journeys far from home.

questions.prompt: Arthur Dent escapes Earth moments before its demolition and travels through space with his friend Ford Prefect.
options: The Restaurant at the End of the Universe
The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy

book.title: The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy
book.author: Douglas Adams

questions.explanation: Arthur’s rescue begins an absurd journey through the galaxy.

questions.prompt: Astronaut Mark Watney is left behind on Mars and relies on his scientific training to stay alive.
questions.explanation: Watney’s improvised survival efforts centre the story on Mars.

questions.prompt: A man wakes aboard a spacecraft with almost no memory and gradually discovers that his mission could save humanity.
questions.explanation: Ryland Grace must recover the purpose of his mission while solving its scientific puzzle.

questions.prompt: Rosemary joins the Wayfarer, a wormhole-building ship whose crew brings together people from several species.
options: The Galaxy, and the Ground Within
The Long Way to a Small, Angry Planet

book.title: The Long Way to a Small, Angry Planet
book.author: Becky Chambers

questions.explanation: The Wayfarer’s working life and its varied crew shape Chambers’s space adventure.

questions.prompt: Breq was once the intelligence of a vast starship. Now confined to one human body, she pursues a mission of revenge.
questions.explanation: Leckie’s novel follows the surviving fragment of the starship Justice of Toren.

editions.title: The people we find
editions.intro: A household, a neighbourhood, a circle. Five ways to belong.

questions.prompt: Caseworker Linus Baker is sent to inspect an island home where six unusually magical children live.
options: Miss Peregrine’s Home for Peculiar Children
The Very Secret Society of Irregular Witches
The House in the Cerulean Sea

book.title: The House in the Cerulean Sea
book.author: TJ Klune

questions.explanation: Linus’s assignment brings him into the household run by Arthur Parnassus.

questions.prompt: Mika Moon accepts an invitation to teach three young witches who live together at a place called Nowhere House.
options: The Very Secret Society of Irregular Witches

book.title: The Very Secret Society of Irregular Witches
book.author: Sangu Mandanna

questions.explanation: The invitation challenges Mika’s expectation that witches must live separately.

questions.prompt: A gruff widower’s strictly ordered days are disrupted when Parvaneh and her family move in next door.
options: The Unlikely Pilgrimage of Harold Fry
questions.explanation: Ove’s encounters with his neighbours gradually reveal the person behind his gruff exterior.

questions.prompt: Four residents of a retirement village meet to discuss unsolved crimes, then find themselves investigating a fresh murder.
options: Vera Wong’s Unsolicited Advice for Murderers
questions.explanation: The friends’ weekly meetings become unexpectedly practical when a real case arrives.

questions.prompt: Widowed aquarium cleaner Tova forms an unlikely friendship with Marcellus, a giant Pacific octopus.
questions.explanation: Tova and Marcellus’s connection brings companionship and new possibilities into her life.
